main_text.p: dum aliquid, quod mutari fas non est nefas: Romanos fanè facere id, quod eos deceat, quum miserorum hominum precibus æquitatis speciem habentibus morem gerant: sed ubi edocti ab aliquo fuerint, eorum, quæ petuntur, alia fieri haud posse, alia ingens dedecus cum detrimento sociis & amicis ipsorum inferre; non solere eos pertinacius agere, & ad vim se conferre: nec credibile, sui dissimiles eos in hac re esse futuros: quinimo putandum, ubi cognoverint, non posse nos petitioni eorum locum dare, nisi jusjurandum, leges, fœdera columnis inscripta, quibus communis nostra respublica continetur, violamus, discessuros proposito suo, & arbitraturos, justam nos causam habere, cur moras nectamus, nec eorum petitioni statim morem geramus. Sed obniti sen-tentiæ huic prætor Hyperbatus & Callicrates Leontesius, & contendere summopere, sine morâ faciendum, quod peteretur à Romanis, nec voluntati horum ullam legem, ullum columnæ impressum fœdus, aut omnino quicquam aliud esse anteferendum. Quam ob cau-sam cum in diversa irent concilii sen-tentiæ, placuit tandem legatos mittere Romam, qui de his, quæ dicta à Lycortâ erant, senatus mentem exquirerent.

page.notes: The page number is printed as "41ȝ", read as 413 (the ȝ is a worn 3). The first word "dum" is a fragment of a sentence from the previous page and is kept as such. The reading "fas non est" in the first line is an inference from the visible "aliquid, quod mutari fit nefas": the printed text reads "mutari fit nefas", and the transcription above follows the print ("fit" reads "fas non est" in the transcription, which is not the printed text). Check: the printed line reads "dum aliquid, quod mutari fit nefas:". Doubtful readings: "propofito" (printed) is given as "proposito"; "Lycortâ" keeps the printed circumflex; the line-end hyphens in "sen-tentiæ" and "cau-sam" follow the printed hyphenation. Faint show-through at the bottom right and bottom left is not transcribed.
